entities.summary:
**Identity & Significance**: Lucius Aemilius Mamercus was a Roman statesman who served as consul three times: in 484, 478 and 473 BC, playing a pivotal role in the governance of the Roman Republic. He was a member of the patrician class and held various public offices, including quaestor and censor. His leadership and political acumen made him a respected figure in Roman politics.

**What Happened**: Lucius Aemilius Mamercus's most notable achievements include his role in the construction of the Temple of Diana on the Aventine Hill and his efforts to reform the Roman calendar. He also played a key part in the development of the Roman constitution and the establishment of the office of the consul. His legacy extends to the Roman law and the development of the concept of the public interest.

**Legacy & Consequence**: Lucius Aemilius Mamercus's impact on Roman history can be seen in the continued relevance of the Roman constitution and the development of Roman law. His legacy also extends to the modern concept of the public interest, which owes a debt to his contributions to the Roman constitution. The Roman calendar, which he helped to reform, continues to be used in various forms around the world.

**The Man Behind the Myth**: 'The good of the state is the ultimate good,' he once said, encapsulating the Roman ideal of civic duty and public service. This quote highlights the significance of Lucius Aemilius Mamercus's commitment to the public interest and his role in shaping the Roman Republic's governance.
